title.value: Isolating the impact of tissue heterogeneities in high dose rate brachytherapy treatment of the breast
title.justification: The title of the paper is clearly stated at the beginning of the abstract and again in the introduction section.
title.quote: Isolating the impact of tissue heterogeneities in high dose rate brachytherapy treatment of the breast ^{☆}

analysis.description: This paper investigates the effects of tissue heterogeneities on dose calculations in high dose rate brachytherapy treatment for breast cancer. The study recalculates treatment plans for 123 patients using Monte Carlo-based treatment planning software, highlighting the differences in dose-volume histogram metrics when tissue-specific scattering is considered.

type.justification: The paper reports on an empirical study involving the recalculation of treatment plans for actual patient data using Monte Carlo-based treatment planning software.
type.quote: In this work, the effects of this assumption on calculated dose were investigated by comparing dose to water in water (D w,w ) in an unbound phantom mimicking TG-43 conditions, and dose to medium in medium (D m,m ) for breast cancer patients treated with high dose rate brachytherapy.

name.justification: The research focuses on recalculating radiotherapy treatment plans with a focus on physics-based methods and computations, which places it in the domain of Medical Physics.
name.quote: Clinical brachytherapy treatment planning is performed assuming the patient is composed entirely of water and infinite in size.

name.justification: Brachytherapy is the specific application discussed in the treatment of breast cancer using radiation oncology techniques.
name.quote: In APBI delivered with high dose rate (HDR) brachytherapy, 34 Gy in 10 fractions is prescribed to the tumor bed post-lumpectomy.

name.justification: The study makes extensive use of Monte Carlo simulations for dose calculation, highlighting the importance of this method.
name.quote: Calculations were performed by using a validated treatment planning software, RapidBrachyMCTPS [25], with an MC dose calculation engine based on Geant4 [30,31].
